To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Optoelectronic implementations of parallel processing systems are more cost-effective and have higher performance than their VLSI counterparts.
optoelectronic devices can provide high bandwidth, low volume and high speed processing.

(1) optoelectronic interconnection networks are superior to VLSI interconnection networks, (2) the optoelectronics interconnection networks are based on expander graph topologies, and (3) the smart spatial light modulator (smart-SLM) technology provides an ideal implementation of the expander graph interconnection networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of massively parallel processing systems that are cost-effective, scalable, fault tolerant and high performance.
the study of the design trade-offs and the technological feasibility of optoelectronic massively parallel processing systems.
the development of a design methodology which is based on the use of smart-SLMs for massively parallel computing and communication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
optoelectronic interconnections are the most promising approach to massively parallel computing.
smart spatial light modulators (SSLMs), which can be used to build optoelectronic devices, are the key components for massively parallel processing systems.
optoelectronic devices are a viable technology for massively parallel processing systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optoelectrically-based massively parallel processing systems have the potential to be the most cost-effective, high performance systems.
optoelectronic interconnections are more efficient than electrical interconnections and smart pixels/smart SLMs based optoelectronics systems are more efficient than VLSI systems.
optoelectronic interconnections are more bandwidth efficient than VLSI interconnections and smart pixels are more bandwidth efficient that smart spatial light modulators.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of smart spatial light modulators in the design of massively parallel optoelectronic processing systems can provide significant advantages in performance, volume, and power consumption over VLSI implementations.
optoelectronic devices are a promising technology to implement massively parallel processing systems.
optoelectronic devices can be used in massively parallel processing systems with high performance and low cost.
